name: What kind of filtration works best with a saltwater pool?

mainEntity.name: Should a saltwater pool use cartridge, sand, or DE filtration for the best long-term results?
mainEntity.text: Should a saltwater pool use cartridge, sand, or DE filtration for the best long-term results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Saltwater pools can use cartridge, sand, or DE filtration, but the best option depends on the homeowner’s priorities. Cartridge filters are often easier to maintain and avoid backwashing, while sand filters can be simpler and more affordable upfront. DE filters can provide very fine filtration but may require more attention. What matters most is that the filter is properly sized for the pool and paired with a circulation system that keeps water moving efficiently. A salt generator does not replace good filtration; it depends on it. In Los Angeles, where dust, heat, and regular pool use can cloud water quickly, filtration quality matters a lot. When reviewing a design, ask how the filter size was chosen, how often it will need cleaning, and whether the system is designed for easy service access. The best choice is the one that fits the pool, the budget, and the owner’s maintenance style.
acceptedAnswer.description: Saltwater systems can work with cartridge, sand, or DE filters, but the best choice depends on budget, maintenance preference, and water clarity goals. The filter should match the pool’s turnover needs and the circulation design, not the salt system by itself. Good filtration helps the generator work more efficiently.
